reviews.text: Has little new to say about human greed but the acting and comic observation is superb
reviews.author: Geoffrey Macnab

reviews.text: As a satire on fashion and the super-rich, Ruben Östlund’s Triangle of Sadness has its moments, but isn’t entertaining or incisive enough to fully work.
reviews.author: Daniel Allen

reviews.text: For those who value smart class commentary, wrapped in top notch production design and entertainment, then “Triangle of Sadness” is one that’ll repulse the eyes but greatly satisfy the mind.
reviews.author: Calum Cooper

reviews.text: No more interesting or enlightening than your average troll pointing out that you, too, live in a society.
reviews.author: Joonatan Itkonen

reviews.text: Despite some fascinating performances from Charlbi Dean Kriek and Woody Harrelson, director Ruben Östlund bites off more than he can chew and struggles to digest it.
reviews.author: Tamma Moksha

reviews.text: I didn’t hate it…I just didn’t love it, the last act felt like it was spinning its wheels
reviews.author: Avaryl Halley

reviews.text: I was rolling on the floor laughing
reviews.author: Andrew Galdi

reviews.text: Although at times the charisma of Woody Harrelson can smooth the waters, this movie does not have the intelligence of Parasite -with which it has certain thematic links-, but neither has the audacity of the films of Radu Jude. [Full review in Spanish]
reviews.author: Nicolás Medina

reviews.text: Ruben Östlund cements himself as the people’s satirist. Laying bare an incendiary critique of the 1% that never pats itself on the back, instead being the rare epic that invites its audience to take part in its blistering dismantlement of the idle rich.
reviews.author: Prabhjot Bains

reviews.text: Bitter, clever and absolutely on the money.
reviews.author: Stephanie Bunbury

reviews.text: Even though Triangle of Sadness is entertaining, Östlund could’ve taken more steps to criticise the shallowness of wealthy people and social media influencers.
reviews.author: Nuha Hassan

reviews.text: "Gilligan's Island" holds up as a better example of the left roasting right-wing capitalist pigs, whose greed knows no sliver of human decency.
reviews.author: Cole Smithey

reviews.text: The surprising turn of events in Triangle of Sadness leads to an inevitable conclusion; power is the ultimate form of currency, and even the lowliest of dictators will do whatever it takes to hang onto it.
reviews.author: Paul Kanieski

reviews.text: "Triangle of Sadness" is a true artist's take on people's twisted behavior when they know they have leverage.
reviews.author: Matthew Creith

reviews.text: The target of Ruben Östlund’s latest class satire is a takedown of the tone-deaf rich on the high seas. Unfortunately, this satire doesn’t challenge the status quo but flatters like-minded individuals thoughts on class and wealth.
reviews.author: Jillian Chilingerian

reviews.text: This satirical late capitalist parable about the rich’s intolerant food chain and gender roles is never detained by the sledgehammer procedure of its creator.
reviews.author: Hector A. Gonzalez

reviews.text: Triangle of Sadness loses credibility by backing off in the film’s final moments. We’re left with a cliffhanger, a reminder of the limits Östlund could have gone to.
reviews.author: Tina Kakadelis

reviews.text: If at times its gross out humour can prove a bit too much, the razor sharp script and timely subject matter keep it a constantly engaging film that rarely feels its runtime.
reviews.author: Christopher Connor

reviews.text: I found it to be far too obvious and much too long; it's nowhere near as searing and subtle as Östlund's 'Force Majeure,' which had an emotional sting.
reviews.author: Jeffrey M. Anderson

reviews.text: As was the case with Force Majeure (and not so much the case with The Square), Triangle of Sadness is funny, at times outrageously so.
reviews.author: David Bax

reviews.text: It’s a wild satire of the mega-wealthy and the people who serve them.
reviews.author: Rudie Obias

reviews.text: 'Triangle of Sadness' kicks up the wild meter and delivers a more narratively scattered work [compared to Östlund’s previous films]. Still, it hangs in the mind and is intelligent filmmaking.
reviews.author: Preston Barta

reviews.text: This year a good Scandinavian director shows many things I have observed in real life but never once seen depicted on screen and he gets castigated for it.
reviews.author: A.S. Hamrah

reviews.text: Despite the spiciness of its ingredients, this feature film becomes the equivalent of a frustrating three-course meal that gradually disenchants the palate. [Full review in Spanish]
reviews.author: Antonio G. Spíndola

reviews.text: There is a point where all good intentions in a storyline turn to dust, and that is when the said narrative stops respecting its characters, however vile they are.
reviews.author: Milana Vujkov

reviews.text: Its satire sinks into a cocktail of stereotypical and unfunny characters that only work on the surface to build an basic social text about the human condition and the class divergence implanted by the verticality of capitalism. [Full review in Spanish]
reviews.author: Yasser Medina

reviews.text: Malevolent pleasures [are] exhibited...
reviews.author: Robert W. Butler

reviews.text: A scathing stab at class divides.
reviews.author: Namrata Joshi

reviews.text: Triangle of Sadness is a thoroughly entertaining, delightfully wicked fable about structures of power that are only one shipwreck away from going belly up. A perfect parable for an age of excess.
reviews.author: Saibal Chatterjee

reviews.text: Ostlund doesn’t want to eat the rich; he wants to eat with them.
reviews.author: Elissa Suh

reviews.text: If you have the stomach for it, Triangle of Sadness is the comedy of the year so far. No contest.
reviews.author: Graeme Tuckett

reviews.text: There's something bracingly right, even crowd-pleasing, about the plot's final twist. It may not be uplifting Oscar material, but this satire is seaworthy.
reviews.author: Margot Harrison

reviews.text: Östlund always employs an insolent outlook, laughing at his characters, judging them for their thoughts and actions, making fun of their reactions and contradictions, and showing off their baseness. [Full review in Spanish]
reviews.author: Diego Batlle

reviews.text: Exhilarating at its best and worthy of reflection even at its most obvious and narrow.
reviews.author: Matt Pais

reviews.text: In this exercise in unbridled misanthropy, cinema seems to fade into the background. [Full review in Spanish]
reviews.author: Alejandro Lingenti

reviews.text: Perhaps too long, the uneven film starts out high and above but ends up somewhere beneath. [Full review in Spanish]
reviews.author: Pablo O. Scholz

reviews.text: Despite the sharp satirical tone, some biting observations, and the use of some clever visual metaphors, Östlund repeatedly lapses into the obvious... and is barely saved by his craft and, of course, his indisputable talent. [Full review in Spanish]
reviews.author: Alfonso Flores-Durón y Martínez

reviews.text: It is a film full of demagogy and social resentment whose darts are overwhelmingly obvious. [Full review in Spanish]
reviews.author: Alejandro Alemán

reviews.text: Set on a luxury cruise, this dark comedy feels like a psychological experiment crossed with the gross-out humor of 'Jackass.'
reviews.author: Gavia Baker-Whitelaw

reviews.text: Between period dramas and meta-cinematic reflections, here's a hilarious and shameless parody. [Full review in Spanish]
reviews.author: Randy Meeks

reviews.text: The virtue of the Swede's gaze is in his ability to turn each daily act into the result of infinite meticulously ordered errors. [Full review in Spanish]
reviews.author: Luis Martínez

reviews.text: Triangle of Sadness is the best manifestation of a current trend (although Öslund has always practiced it): the sharp satire saturated with black humor geared towards the rich. [Full review in Spanish]
reviews.author: Desirée De Fez

reviews.text: It's vulgar, childish and lacking in subtlety, but also a lot of fun. [Full review in Spanish]
reviews.author: Nando Salvá

reviews.text: Not just on the cruise, but in the social hierarchy. Östlund drags them down to earth cruelly, and no champagne can clean this new stench.
reviews.author: Brian Susbielles

reviews.text: Watching this brazen satire is quite a singular experience. Hilarious and well-acted but also overlong and as indulgent as the filthy rich aboard the yacht.
reviews.author: Ruth Maramis

reviews.text: ...wicked but weirdly unsubtle social satire...
reviews.author: Rahul Desai

reviews.text: Insofar as originality is concerned - the plot is directly lifted from the British film 'The Admirable Crichton' (1957), based on a J.M. Barrie play...I found this a smug, self-indulgent bore - but, obviously my negative opinion is in the minority.
reviews.author: Susan Granger

reviews.text: Ruben Östlund is proving himself to be a master at creating discomfort by exposing the hypocrisy of the characters he follows. [Full review in Portuguese]
reviews.author: Pablo Villaça

reviews.text: Might have been the picture of the year if it had ended nearly 80 minutes in.
reviews.author: Sonny Bunch

reviews.text: Best projectile vomiting of 2022.
reviews.author: Robert Roten

reviews.text: 'Triangle of Sadness' satirizes high society's self-obsessed elites, making for a side-splitting, vomit-spewing, hilariously unhinged time.
reviews.author: Morgan Rojas

reviews.text: Money can't buy you a solution to basic bodily functions when food poisoning and seasickness strike, and doesn't this scathingly entertaining flick revel in that notion at its most gleefully gross.
reviews.author: Sarah Ward

reviews.text: A painfully blunt satire of the super rich and Instagram celebrity that is rarely entertaining and often annoying.
reviews.author: Aaron White

reviews.text: Östlund's new order... showcasing people appearing sophisticated (and failing). [Full review in Spanish]
reviews.author: Fernanda Solórzano

reviews.text: A surprisingly accessible yet deeply profound social commentary. The first act explores evolving gender dynamics, the second act spews seasick political satire aboard a luxury yacht, and the third act becomes a “Lord of the Flies” survivalist allegory.
reviews.author: Jason Fraley

reviews.text: The title doesn’t effectively sell how chaotically funny and eviscerating Ruben Ostlund’s social satire is.
reviews.author: Wenlei Ma

reviews.text: Dark satiric take on the uber rich and ridiculously influential from a filmmaker with a wicked eye and ear for how we behave, and a gift for sending us up
reviews.author: Jane Freebury

reviews.text: The crude nature of the director’s anti-materialist message – not far removed from a piece of unregenerate Marxism – is redeemed by his craftsmanship and black sense of humour.
reviews.author: John McDonald

reviews.text: Östlund is a mad genius; he's a mad scientist of cinema that philosophizes with celluloid. He's blunt and brutal with his satire...
reviews.author: Alex Billington

reviews.text: The mere fact that the audience applauds a harsh look in the mirror of ego-driven monsters brings a whole new meaning to the phrase if you look around the room and don’t see the sucker, you’re it.
reviews.author: M.N. Miller

reviews.text: Both viciously funny and heartbreaking.
reviews.author: James Greenberg

reviews.text: Charlbi Dean made waves with her performance...
reviews.author: Fletcher Peters

reviews.text: He makes astute observations about small social niceties, but he pushes every awkward situation to the point where viewers gasp and wince.
reviews.author: Nicholas Barber

reviews.text: Survival is a dark art in Swedish film-maker Ruben Östlund’s trenchant shipwreck satire.
reviews.author: Andiee Paviour

reviews.text: There’s an interesting cast of mostly unknown actors (Harrelson excepted) and the film is very well staged. Maybe the Cannes accolade was a bit on the generous side, though.
reviews.author: David Stratton

reviews.text: Östlund has some great ideas, but it almost seems his goal is to intentionally push the joke beyond its limits of insufferability.
reviews.author: Jared Mobarak

reviews.text: What starts out as a ripping, hot-blooded social satire skewering wealth, insta-fame and class snobbery dies almost exactly half-way through...What a pity that something that begins so witty and dry should end up so witless and wet.
reviews.author: Jim Schembri

reviews.text: For Östlund, subtlety is overrated. Triangle of Sadness shows us why he has a point. It’s a spectacular demolition of modern life, a disruptor movie full of ideas and nuance, as violent in its way as a Pieter Bruegel painting.
reviews.author: Paul Byrnes

reviews.text: The now infamous dinner scene, that resulted in numerous walkouts at Cannes -- the same festival at which the film took home the coveted Palme d'Or -- will make or break it for many, depending how strong their stomachs.
reviews.author: Kat Halstead

reviews.text: In a manner a bit too similar to its ignorant bourgeois characters, Triangle of Sadness is content to sit back and gawk at surface-level misery without incisively looking deeper.
reviews.author: Eliza Janssen

reviews.text: These people have all the entitlement and self-awareness of pre-Revolutionary French aristocrats, and Östlund keenly exposes their vicious decadence to a disgusting degree, especially as a storm arrives to reveal the extent of the mass hubris.
reviews.author: Andrea Thompson

reviews.text: Triangle of Sadness doesn’t leave audiences with much to unpack thematically, but it’s clear-eyed and hilarious about the systems that enforce societal inequities and what might happen if they were ever to unravel.
reviews.author: Scott Tobias

reviews.text: I get what it’s trying to achieve, but the attempts to be of-so-clever yield a pretentious garbage trough.
reviews.author: Kevin Carr

reviews.text: Not nearly as subversive as it could or should be, but there's little out there that can top the Centrepiece of Spew.
reviews.author: Simon Miraudo

reviews.text: If you're looking for a film that conveys its main themes through subtext, don't even try to watch it. But if you are willing to have a disruptive and ruthless experience that's a tad overlong, "Triangle of Sadness" is an excellent option.
reviews.author: Sebastian Zavala Kahn

reviews.text: A boring and nauseating movie.
reviews.author: Jackie K. Cooper

reviews.text: … has its moments of brilliance, but at heart, it is a blunt instrument.
reviews.author: Nadine Whitney

reviews.text: While the satire is pompous and at times buoyed by goofy humor, it is entertaining and worth watching.  [Full review in Spanish]
reviews.author: Ruben Peralta Rigaud

reviews.text: Triangle of Sadness is far from subtle about what it wants to say, but it is hard to resist its depiction of wealthy, powerful and beautiful people as they are stripped of dignity and autonomy.
reviews.author: Thomas Caldwell

reviews.text: Östlund sets his eyes squarely on deserved targets and dismantles them with satirical wit and sophistication, making “Triangle of Sadness” one of the smartest and most interesting films of the year.
reviews.author: Louisa Moore

reviews.text: The rich are an easy target, but ever a worthy one, and Triangle of Sadness stirs enough eff-the-ruling-class righteousness to warrant a watch... but this recommendation hinges on the strength of your stomach.
reviews.author: John Serba

reviews.text: In the new film, reflecting the force of processes too obvious to be ignored, Östlund has expanded his scope. The English-language film is uneven, but its skewering of capitalism is certainly welcome.
reviews.author: David Walsh

reviews.text: An incisive and insightful film that puts its finger on the wound of the capitalist system. [Full review in Spanish]
reviews.author: Emiliano Basile

reviews.text: It’s a raft that thinks it’s a cruise ship. It floats, but it doesn’t hold nearly as much as it thinks it does.
reviews.author: Cory Woodroof

reviews.text: Triangle of Sadness is a black comedy whose satirical view of the uber-rich leads to some true laugh out loud moments. The film takes a while to get going... but the film’s final act is well worth the wait.
reviews.author: Mark Johnson

reviews.text: “Triangle of Sadness” completes Östlund’s triptych about men and money, but with a third act that feels like a minor deflation, dialing down the film’s absurdities in favor of more literal and didactic extrications.
reviews.author: Siddhant Adlakha

reviews.text: Triangle of Sadness is more than a little over the top at times. But so what? Unlike every other movie at the theaters, it’s over the top in its scathing portrayal of the ugly realities of contemporary inequality.
reviews.author: Eileen Jones

reviews.text: What remains so impressive about Triangle of Sadness is how Östlund never resorts to dry didacticism and manages to contain his thought-provoking ideas in a deliriously entertaining experience.
reviews.author: Brian Eggert

reviews.text: There's a lot to like, but a sharper and more focused approach would have made "Triangle of Sadness" less square.
reviews.author: Tom Santilli

reviews.text: Triangle of Sadness is the near perfect Dark Comedy! Balancing tone, message, darkness of human nature and equally being one of the funniest films this year!
reviews.author: Samuel Leggett Jr.

reviews.text: Features a great conceit, fantastic set pieces, and some fine character work.
reviews.author: Stephen Silver

reviews.text: Östlund stretches out a few scenes past their expiration date, but the dark social satire is hilarious as it sadly showcases our potential for stupidity. One of the best films of the year.
reviews.author: Joe Friar

reviews.text: Östlund wasn’t smart enough to take some possible good ideas to better conclusions, preferring a cinema that is coarse, drastic and with no consequence. It can be funny at times, though.
reviews.author: Filipe Freitas

reviews.text: If, within 149 minutes, all you can do is point at people and laugh at their emptiness and shallow behavior, then your thesis sadly embodies a similar vacancy.
reviews.author: Michael Ward

reviews.text: Östlund reveals himself to be a social satirist and political thinker on the level of Adam McKay, and just as inexplicably acclaimed.
reviews.author: Sean Burns

reviews.text: Shirking any of the more subtle dynamics of Force Majeure, this is a cold observation of the human condition, but told with such consistent originality, that the runtime is almost justified.
reviews.author: Gemma Creagh

reviews.text: There is scarcely a gag or scenario that isn’t telegraphed and obvious, and yet it’s seemingly just as satisfied with its own cleverness as its targets are with their over-pampered, empty lives.
reviews.author: Adam Kempenaar

reviews.text: Triangle of Sadness reckons with a timeless issue in an erratic and ultimately unsatisfying feature.
reviews.author: Matt Conway

reviews.text: [It] made its point in the first couple of minutes and then proceeded to go on for two-and-a-half hours.
reviews.author: Jason Shawhan

reviews.text: Triangle of Sadness is a hilarious and thought-provoking film, which manages to nail its satirical tone and commentary on classism, until the moment it manages to fall apart.
reviews.author: Theolin Tembo

reviews.text: A bit on the nose, perhaps, but an anarchic, thought-provoking romp, all the same.
reviews.author: Hilary A White

reviews.text: ...the movie’s overall impact is dulled significantly by a ludicrously overlong running time (149 minutes!)...
reviews.author: David Nusair

reviews.text: You can – just about – pity Carl, even whilst being eminently frustrated by him, and held apart from him. This is a film which leaves some big questions hanging without compromising on its verve and wit.
reviews.author: Keri O'Shea

reviews.text: “Triangle of Sadness” boasts of being deep and smart but in reality, it is an arrogant display of cartoonish, lazy, basic writing. [Full Review in Spanish]
reviews.author: Ricardo Gallegos

reviews.text: There's great heady stuff going on and also really weird fun in this film too.
reviews.author: tt stern-enzi

reviews.text: Yes, the metaphor can seem very on-the-nose: the super rich, in this economic climate especially, are obscene and repulsive! But it's a film of great subtlety (really) and benefits from multiple viewings.
reviews.author: Kevin Maher

reviews.text: A wicked, at-times horrifically and humorously gross, satire that takes aim at the wealthy in a manner that is deliciously void of any subtlety.
reviews.author: Peter Gray

reviews.text: Swedish director Ruben Östlund takes no prisoners in his satirical approach.
reviews.author: Wendy Ide

reviews.text: The relish of the attack, the invention of the imminent mortifications and the cool precision of Östlund’s filmmaking rescues Triangle of Sadness.
reviews.author: Donald Clarke

reviews.text: Triangle of Sadness is certainly a blunt and audacious film with its brittle outlook of the affluent
reviews.author: Latoya Austin

reviews.text: It’s a sweet revenge dream for those of us who have to work for a living without a lot to show for it, and Östlund brings it to vivid life with caustic wit.
reviews.author: Gena Radcliffe

reviews.text: Like The Square, Triangle Of Sadness rather outstays its welcome. But also like The Square, it contains at least one scene that, without wanting to go similarly overboard myself, deserves nothing less than cinematic immortality.
reviews.author: Brian Viner

reviews.text: The film is a collection of thought bubbles aimlessly circling each other in hope they will cohere and preference character development over amusing but pointless oddities.
reviews.author: Damien Straker

reviews.text: It is all very clear cut to the point of being oddly safe, and the film rapidly starts to feel like it is straining to make some sort of deeper meaning out of this.
reviews.author: Chase Hutchinson

reviews.text: As much as Östlund wants to be the Ari Aster of elevated black comedy, Triangle of Sadness is — if I may borrow a Patton Oswalt punchline — a failure pile in a sadness bowl.
reviews.author: Craig D. Lindsey

reviews.text: Östlund’s blunderbuss satire is not subtle... But it’s also very funny in a bleak sort of way, and the scenes on the boat mid-storm are at once hilarious and repellent.
reviews.author: Paul Whitington

reviews.text: For a film that hilariously skewers the excesses of the ultra-rich, “Triangle” also feels like too much — too long, too obvious, too gross.
reviews.author: Rob Thomas

reviews.text: Triangle of Sadness is very strange and might not be everyone's cup of tea, but if you loved White Lotus and satire aimed at the beautiful and rich, this is a definite must-watch. The fact that it won the Palme d'Or is in itself almost satirical...
reviews.author: Gabi Zietsman

reviews.text: Östlund is shooting fish in a barrel here, but if his targets are glaring, there's at least some fun to be had along the way.
reviews.author: Adam Graham

reviews.text: Most comfortable in its all-out blaze of high fashion, yachts, expensive food, and jewellery, the film’s cynicism and formal sleight-of-hand lacquer over any sense of radical political excitement.
reviews.author: Georgie Carr

reviews.text: One already notorious sequence aside, Triangle of Sadness feels a little like gnashing at air.
reviews.author: Clarisse Loughrey

reviews.text: A messy satire about wealth that occasionally uses a scalpel — but more often a scattergun.
reviews.author: Danny Leigh

reviews.text: Östlund needs someone like my mother in his life to tell him it’s not clever, it’s not funny, pack it in.
reviews.author: Deborah Ross

reviews.text: Some may love it and some may hate it, but I can’t deny that it was an engrossing watch.
reviews.author: Collier Jennings

reviews.text: At nearly two and a half hours long, Triangle of Sadness' satiric aims just can't sustain the weight of its own ambitions.
reviews.author: Mattie Lucas

reviews.text: ...a bit too pleased with itself and pitiless.
reviews.author: Josh Larsen

reviews.text: Östlund bungles the political, spiritual, and moral lessons of such classics about chaos as Luis Buñuel’s Exterminating Angel, Antonioni’s L’Avventura, and Godard’s Weekend.
reviews.author: Armond White

reviews.text: When a director’s brand is cynicism, every choice can seem calculated for effect over meaning.
reviews.author: Ryan Gilbey

reviews.text: Triangle of Sadness is ultimately a cautionary tale where the moral of the story is that power corrupts.
reviews.author: Michelle Kisner

reviews.text: It’s not exactly subtle, but it is funny, thanks largely to the emetic chaos of its set-at-sea second act and a series of sly turns from its up-for-anything international cast.
reviews.author: Alistair Harkness

reviews.text: Despite Ruben Östlund’s shortcomings and imprudent tropes, Triangle of Sadness is harrowing, consistently funny, and packed with surprises.
reviews.author: Maxwell Rabb

reviews.text: While there are glints of Ostlund’s uncomfortable brilliance, overall, this send-up of over-consumption feels obvious.
reviews.author: Alison Gillmor

reviews.text: Triangle invites us to feel bad about ourselves, and, in doing so, we end up celebrating the very things it criticizes. We end up admiring the movie from a distance, like it’s a model in a runway show that’s projecting Karl Marx quotes on the rear wall.
reviews.author: Neal Pollack

reviews.text: Expect much mayhem and let the good times roll.
reviews.author: Christopher Llewellyn Reed

reviews.text: An absurd, iconoclastic riot. Ruben Östlund’s point may be blunt — yep, rich people are bad — but his telling of it is hilariously, breathlessly entertaining.
reviews.author: John Nugent

reviews.text: To me, the most intriguing aspect of Triangle of Sadness was the concept of personal worth and social power assigned to both money and beauty.
reviews.author: Peg Aloi

reviews.text: The film is on the lengthy side, but it is every bit as ambitious and bracingly entertaining.
reviews.author: Jeremy Aspinall

reviews.text: By its finish, Triangle of Sadness’s bluntness transforms itself into an avenue to more compelling, less facile questions than it asked closer to its start, more reliable throughout as a fount of commentary than of social comment.
reviews.author: George Elkind

reviews.text: Swedish writer-director Ruben Ostlund makes his English-language debut with this funny, sharply observed work after a string of well-received comedy-dramas that put middle-class characters in a pickle.
reviews.author: John Lui

reviews.text: Östlund gives us plenty to absorb as he runs his filthy rich subjects through the wringer. Some scenes are savagely funny while others are simply savage. More importantly, we’re always engaged.
reviews.author: Keith Garlington

reviews.text: As was the case with The Square, Triangle of Sadness takes some time to get going and occasionally slips into pretentiousness, but on this occasion Ostlund’s screenplay is better focused.
reviews.author: James Berardinelli

reviews.text: This delightfully scathing satire targets the obscenely wealthy as well as the working class, but also delves into how youth and beauty are commodities with expiration dates.
reviews.author: Frank J. Avella

reviews.text: Ultimately, de Leon is not enough to save this overpraised satire that somehow is at its best during its most outrageous and disgusting moments.
reviews.author: Jas Keimig

reviews.text: With hilarious performances from Harrison Dickinson and Woody Harrelson, and a star-making turn by Dolly de Leon, Triangle of Sadness is one of those movies that keeps getting funnier as it sinks lower and lower.
reviews.author: Jennifer Heaton

reviews.text: This take on "Titanic" by way of "Das Kapital" and "Gilligan's Island," which admittedly does have its pleasures, has about as much subtlety as a falling coconut.
reviews.author: Cary Darling

reviews.text: Never boring, which is an achievement in and of itself, but the lack of follow-through leaves you wondering whether Östlund’s feints towards social issues came out of genuine curiosity or if they were just more clever tricks of imagery.
reviews.author: Vincent Mancini

reviews.text: Östlund’s brilliantly arch sense of humour, bold willingness to extend the embarrassment or excruciation level of a scene to breaking point, and talent for memorable, emotionally immersive set pieces are certainly on display.
reviews.author: Demetrios Matheou

reviews.text: Triangle of Sadness is a scathing takedown of influencers & wealth hoarders, the most deranged episode of Below Deck Bravo wishes they produced.
reviews.author: Graeme Guttmann

reviews.text: Ostlund picks an easy, if worthy, target that teeters satire like the obvious allegory of its centerpiece sequence while getting direct hits and making sure we notice the bullseye before its next shot leading to a final act that ultimately sinks it.
reviews.author: Erik Childress

reviews.text: The sum total of the film’s chapters equals a general portrait of petty human cruelty more than any distinct class analysis.
reviews.author: Joshua Bogatin

reviews.text: The story feels timeless, in large part due to the great performances littered throughout. What feels like a slight step down for Östlund would be many filmmakers’ best film.
reviews.author: Alan French

reviews.text: Triangle of Sadness is social satire of the highest order.
reviews.author: Mike McGranaghan

reviews.text: This is being called a satire, but satires -- theoretically -- should at least make you laugh.
reviews.author: Wade Major

reviews.text: Triangle of Sadness amounts to a good time at the movies (never mind the excessive 149-minute length). Just don’t expect a Karl Marx-calibre critique of capitalism. The film just makes fun of its many excesses and absurdities.
reviews.author: Jorge Ignacio Castillo

reviews.text: Triangle of Sadness pulls off the very difficult trick of changing shape entirely for each of its three acts without losing any personality, cohesion, or humor, or sight of its primary targets.
reviews.author: Nathaniel Rogers

reviews.text: ... becomes bloated and obvious in its second half, with its surface cynicism failing to yield deeper insight beyond its provocative ideas.
reviews.author: Todd Jorgenson

reviews.text: Laughter gives way to groans, groans give way to gasps, and gasps give way to shamed introspection as these colorful caricatures, even in their ivory towers, begin to feel just like us.
reviews.author: Dan Scully

reviews.text: An uneven and superficial film, with some of its class-war satires not that funny.
reviews.author: Dennis Schwartz

reviews.text: As redundant and dependent on its own characters’ farfetched stupidity for its premise as it is... I weirdly enjoyed this popcorn arthouse film.
reviews.author: Rich Juzwiak

reviews.text: Ship of Fools meets Lord of the Flies.
reviews.author: James Verniere

reviews.text: Ostlund trades in outrageous ideas with razored precision, so these 150 minutes are always compelling. At the same time, his satire is relatively heavy-handed this time...
reviews.author: Dennis Harvey

reviews.text: It’s brash, vulgar, often gleefully mean-spirited, and about as subtle as a brick through the window of Neiman Marcus– and it’s exactly what I needed to see.
reviews.author: Oscar Goff

reviews.text: Vulgarians save the biggest gross-out for last. Östlund dabbles in that world, then decides he would rather say something important than wallow any further. The ironic thing is that the commitment to bad taste might have led to added significance.
reviews.author: Alan Zilberman

reviews.text: TRIANGLE OF SADNESS is the sort of overlong, pretentious claptrap that valiant critics the world over get paid to see… so that you don’t have to.
reviews.author: Daniel M. Kimmel

reviews.text: I’m much more fascinated by a movie that aims high and misses rather than one that settles for average.
reviews.author: Allen Almachar

reviews.text: Flawed though it may be -- and why must a film be “perfect”? -- Triangle remains a welcome addition to the Östlund canon. Having picked up tidbits about his next project -- likely a demolition of the donor class -- I’m prepared to love it.
reviews.author: Erica Abeel

reviews.text: It’s not so much that all the characters are so unsympathetic. It’s that they’re all so uninteresting. Caricature without gusto is shrink wrap covering . . . shrink wrap.
reviews.author: Mark Feeney

reviews.text: Instead of skipping lightly over rough seas, Triangle of Sadness bobs to shore like a floating sarcophagus.
reviews.author: Marjorie Baumgarten

reviews.text: As always with Östlund, his most profligate flights of fancy tack close enough to reality to ring queasily true.
reviews.author: Ann Hornaday

reviews.text: Another lively provocation from Swedish filmmaker Ruben Ostlund, this pitch-black comedy overflows as big ideas are laced through an ambitiously epic tale.
reviews.author: Rich Cline

reviews.text: Ruben Östlund’s latest brainy satire is a continually self-renewing yet uncompromisingly coherent opus.
reviews.author: Tomris Laffly

reviews.text: it is over long and too skewered in its storytelling.
reviews.author: Robin Clifford

reviews.text: Not since “Bridesmaids” has a scene involving deification and vomiting yielded such hilarious results, but from there “Triangle of Sadness” remains stagnant.
reviews.author: Nate Adams

reviews.text: Triangle of Sadness’s central scene goes on and on, intensifying without abating and never suggesting that order can ever be restored...
reviews.author: Keith Phipps

reviews.text: The rare satire better enjoyed with your brain switched firmly off.
reviews.author: Alistair Ryder

reviews.text: In Ruben Östlund’s satire, the amusements of the moneyed elite belie a foundation of violence, cowardice, and shame.
reviews.author: Andrew Marzoni

reviews.text: It’s a wild ride that takes aim at some pretty easy targets, but makes a few good points and, more importantly, is funny much of the time.
reviews.author: Hannah Brown

reviews.text: After that final breathless shot, rather than walking out chuckling, you may walk away with your own triangle of sadness engaged, brow furrowed, mouth agape, mind whirring. And isn't that kind of rush worth the price of admission?
reviews.author: Kristy Puchko

reviews.text: The film plays like a mash-up of Lina Wertmüller's "Swept Away" and Michael Winterbottom's "Greed" by way of ‘Gilligan’s Island.’
reviews.author: Laura Clifford

reviews.text: Triangle of Sadness is a comparatively minor entry into Östlund’s oeuvre of anti-capitalist works, but it is his funniest and most accessible film to date.
reviews.author: Sarah Marrs

reviews.text: The darkly comedic Triangle of Sadness is an incisive satire of social class prejudices and gender-based power dynamics. The cast members' skillful performances outweigh the movie's flaws, such as a story that sometimes rambles and has a vague ending.
reviews.author: Carla Hay

reviews.text: Ostlund's main course arrives during a lengthy, memorable, and often laugh-out-loud second act. That's when it simply, uh, overflows with dishing on wealthy guests aboard a luxury yacht, including a "Captain's Dinner" sequence that may even astound.
reviews.author: John Urbancich

reviews.text: Triangle of Sadness seems hemmed in by its tastefulness... The actors try their best, but Östlund’s insistent conceptual droning overtakes them.
reviews.author: K. Austin Collins

reviews.text: Thanks to whip-smart writing, darkly playful callbacks, and a powerhouse performance from de Leon as Abigail, the movie holds together perfectly. De Leon steals the movie, and rightfully so.
reviews.author: Alejandra Martinez

reviews.text: Amounts to a laboured mash-up of  "Gilligan's Island" and "Lord of the Flies."
reviews.author: Peter Howell

reviews.text: Östlund’s slog of a film is exceptional in the distance it creates between the viewer and its characters and in how comfortable its attempts at causticity actually feel.
reviews.author: Alison Willmore

reviews.text: Östlund has characters and metaphors to bludgeon, and the joie de vivre with which he lays waste to the idle rich and the system that keeps them in caviar and cruelty is amusingly obvious until it’s just obvious.
reviews.author: Ty Burr

reviews.text: For all its scathing moments Triangle of Sadness seems acutely aware that, regardless of how much feces hits the fan, deep down little will change among the rich.
reviews.author: Courtney Small

reviews.text: Suffice to say that Ostlund has a keen sense of the absurdities inherent in our social structures, and the ways in which the tools needed for survival on one island -- Manhattan, say -- would prove woefully inadequate on, for example, Gilligan’s.
reviews.author: Chris Knight

reviews.text: You can fully agree that most “haves” are dreadful, and that the “have nots” deserve much more out of life, and still be exhausted and bored by Triangle of Sadness and its quirky acidity.
reviews.author: Stephanie Zacharek

reviews.text: Östlund is shooting fish in a barrel, but the fish had it coming, and he cooks them up into a tasty meal, complete with sea urchin and squid emulsion on the side.
reviews.author: Brian Tallerico

reviews.text: Östlund uses a lot of striking images throughout the film, but the one of a well-to-do madame slip-sliding across her washroom floor in her expensive undergarments and gaudy jewellery attempting to vomit in the toilet with some dignity tops them for me.
reviews.author: Rachel Ho

reviews.text: Having a ferocious takedown of the rich would be a satisfying substitute for substance here, but for a 2.5 hour movie, there just isn’t enough of either to justify the runtime.
reviews.author: Ryan Silberstein

reviews.text: Ruben Östlund is back in his favorite place – the hotel. Bedrooms, dining rooms, common thoroughfares with balustrades, and a vibe of impermanence and mild dread as he looks through keyholes at couples not quite in tune.
reviews.author: Anne Brodie

reviews.text: Ruben Östund’s audacious Palme d’Or winner skewers modern social mores in a note-perfect satire.
reviews.author: Karen Gordon

reviews.text: Only the fine cast lends life to the movie’s superficial caricatures, even if the hectic, blatant script edges the performances toward the clattery side and Östlund’s precise but stiff direction leaves little room for inventiveness.
reviews.author: Richard Brody

reviews.text: Östlund amazes with his meticulous mise en scène and visual mastery. [Full review in French]
reviews.author: Kevin N. Laforest

reviews.text: Somehow, Östlund balances the reserved and ironic humor with an eruption ... of bodily fluids...
reviews.author: Mark Dujsik

reviews.text: "Triangle of Sadness" is a well-crafted, sly and smart commentary on the superficiality of money, power, and class. It is well worth your time and attention.
reviews.author: Karen M. Peterson

reviews.text: I relished Abigail's power in all her coercive, unsettling breadth.
reviews.author: Li Lai

reviews.text: Don't go in expecting art-house intellectualism. The movie is as loaded with fun as it is with social implications.
reviews.author: Kyle Smith

reviews.text: There are a couple of good scenes... but nothing substantial enough to warrant the two-and-a-half-hour running time.
reviews.author: Glenn Whipp

reviews.text: At almost two and a half hours long, Triangle of Sadness, directed by Ruben Östlund, delivers snickering humor about the disconnectivity and excess of the wealthy.
reviews.author: DarkSkyLady

reviews.text: What holds the wild and winding narrative together is the uniformly excellent acting by the entire ensemble.
reviews.author: Kent Turner

reviews.text: The key to a successful trip is making sure all the guests are happy during the first hour and on the last day, which also sums up Triangle of Sadness‘ quality if you replace “the last day” with “the last scene” and bump one hour up to 80 minutes
reviews.author: Robert Kojder

reviews.text: This, in the end, is a very bad movie, executed with enough visual polish and surface cleverness to fool the Cannes jurors, something Ostlund has done twice. Shame on them!
reviews.author: A.O. Scott

reviews.text: The ideas might not be new, and the targets might be easy, but [Ruben Östlund] has once again made something exceedingly uncomfortable and undeniably entertaining.
reviews.author: Lindsey Bahr

reviews.text: Brace yourself for a scathing comedy that takes aim at the wealthy and the beautiful -- and tosses all decorum overboard without a life vest.
reviews.author: Thelma Adams

reviews.text: In setting up and then obliterating such easy targets, Ostlund has created a self-indulgent and lazy screed that mistakes anger for wit, scolding for irony, and vomit (so much vomit) for gags of actual substance.
reviews.author: Barry Hertz

reviews.text: The film is overlong and a little messy, but it’s also hilarious and features what’s likely the grossest set piece I’ve seen in a movie awarded the Palme d’Or at the Cannes Film Festival.
reviews.author: Aaron Neuwirth

reviews.text: In a somber, often underwhelming season of would-be arthouse hits, the movie is a bona-fide trip: not the funhouse mirror we need for these ridiculous times, maybe, but one we deserve.
reviews.author: Leah Greenblatt

reviews.text: It pummels its points decisively, convincingly and with a ferocity you've just gotta admire.
reviews.author: Randy Myers

reviews.text: For 95 minutes of its 147-minute running time, “Triangle of Sadness” is one of the best movies of the year.
reviews.author: Mick LaSalle

reviews.text: A biting and hilarious indictment of the uber-wealthy and the importance we place on beauty. Some will find it completely horrifying, while others will certainly appreciate the ironies on display.
reviews.author: Jeanne Kaplan

reviews.text:
Östlund creates a small world where class distinctions no longer matter. 
The ensemble cast is completely compelling even if some of the characters are unsavory.
reviews.author: David Kaplan

reviews.text: Ruben Östlund skewers the rich, wealth disparity, and gender dynamics in a wickedly funny black comedy. Triangle of Sadness had me laughing hysterically for the entire runtime. Greedy and narcissistic one-percenters get a drastic comeuppance.
reviews.author: Julian Roman

reviews.text: While it is hilarious in its satire, there is an inconsistency in Triangle of Sadness that might make audiences frown in confusion.
reviews.author: Katie Smith-Wong

reviews.text: The best movie of the year
reviews.author: Fred Topel

reviews.text: Triangle of Sadness is neither as smart nor as interesting as it clearly thinks it is.
reviews.author: Brianna Zigler

reviews.text: Triangle of Sadness has the subtlety of a sledgehammer in its message on excess, but it's an absolute laugh riot.
reviews.author: Jeff Nelson

reviews.text: It’s all fun and games until the s**t literally hits the fan.
reviews.author: Joanna Langfield

reviews.text: Bold, provocative and wickedly funny. Making the audience laugh while making them think and feel is no easy task, but Ruben Östlund accomplishes it with flying colors. Dolly De Leon gives a breakthrough performance.
reviews.author: Avi Offer

reviews.text: Östlund mostly dispenses with subtlety in favor of a raucous sort of precision, setting up his gilded pins for the inevitable bowling ball hurtling at them. One imagines it won the top prize at Cannes for its raw audacity as much as anything else.
reviews.author: Piers Marchant

reviews.text: It's a brilliant, wickedly funny dissection of ego, materialism, social hierarchy, and conventions. It’s a near-perfect satirical work with a fantastic ensemble cast that turns the tables on society’s upper class.
reviews.author: Sara Clements

reviews.text: The experience shifts from being one in which the audience enjoys the nightmare that these terrible people must endure into one in which we must examine our reactions. Suddenly there’s more at stake ...
reviews.author: Barbara Goslawski

reviews.text: It’s easy to see why this year’s Cannes jury was so smitten with what [Östlund] achieves here, even though I hope his next venture will be a tighter and more disciplined affair.
reviews.author: Tomas Trussow

reviews.text: It’s as severe of a collapse as I’ve seen in a highly-acclaimed comedy in quite a while.
reviews.author: Nick Johnston

reviews.text: The Palme d’Or winner lays its satire on thick, but its fun performances (particularly Harris Dickinson) and farcical sense of humour make for an entertaining ride. At times outrageously hilarious, but its messaging is as subtle as a sledgehammer.
reviews.author: Fiona Underhill

reviews.text: This is pointed, barbed humor laser-focused on the beautiful and the avaricious, who can’t seem to imagine the life of people who have to work for a living.
reviews.author: Andy Howell

reviews.text: The jokes are cracklingly dry while sandwiched between toilet gags that make for a rip-roaring experience. Östlund’s work sits comfortably beside the work of Armando Iannucci in its ability to blend sharp and dry wit with over-the-top vulgarity.
reviews.author: Lindsay Traves

reviews.text: Seinfeldian in one moment, Lord of the Flies in the next, Triangle of Sadness manages to accelerate the shock factor up until its final beat.
reviews.author: Hannah Lodge

reviews.text: The third act is stretched out and it slogs its way through, if only for the belief that a movie that isn’t at least 2 hours can’t be taken seriously by the film art community.
reviews.author: Soham Gadre

reviews.text: Triangle of Sadness can be a blunt instrument at times, but it wonderfully weaves its tale of class warfare. It’s a vacation I won’t forget anytime soon.
reviews.author: Max Covill

reviews.text: The middle section is not for the faint of heart and not simply because the satire cuts so deep. A fancy dinner on a luxury yacht into a burlesque of barf so vivid it makes the Mr. Creosote sequence from Monty Python's The Meaning of Life seem restrained.
reviews.author: Richard Crouse

reviews.text: Triangle of Sadness is a premium experience where classist themes and riotous drama are served on a silver platter.
reviews.author: Thomas Stoneham-Judge

reviews.text: Triangle of Sadness offers up a repetitive joke that wears out its welcome very early on.
reviews.author: Joey Magidson

reviews.text: After going all in on gross-out humor in its second act, Triangle of Sadness never recovers in what is one of the weirdest films of 2022.
reviews.author: Danielle Solzman

reviews.text: Writer-director Ruben Östlund’s pessimism ultimately leads the film toward a self-negating dead end.
reviews.author: Keith Watson

reviews.text: A hilarious and occasionally graphic continuation of the recent "eat the rich" picture pantheon.
reviews.author: Matthew St. Clair

reviews.text: Östlund's comedy of inequality and broken class structures might be a bit too blunt at times, slightly too long, and is often best when at its simplest, but Triangle of Sadness is too fun and ridiculous to not enjoy.
reviews.author: Ross Bonaime

reviews.text: It’s frequently gross, blunt as a battering ram, and very, very 2022.
reviews.author: Alissa Wilkinson

reviews.text: Triangle of Sadness is not particularly sophisticated in its critique of late-stage capitalism. That doesn’t stop its gags from being deliriously funny.
reviews.author: Jamie Dunn

reviews.text: There’s no doubt about Östlund’s visual acumen—the camera movement and cinematography cover you in laughing gas—and yet, you’re never quite sure what more Östlund wants to say other than the rich are bad.
reviews.author: Robert Daniels

reviews.text: Triangle of Sadness has no politics beyond gesturing toward extreme wealth and power and saying, “That ain’t right,” and it has no counterpoint to this paradigm which it presents so sneeringly.
reviews.author: Sophie Monks Kaufman

reviews.text: Let’s hope the film’s own award-season trajectory isn’t one that rewards the white folk when a woman of color does the heavy lifting.
reviews.author: Martin Tsai

reviews.text: Deeply outrageous and not remotely subtle in its satirical execution. May be a bit long but overall a great watch.
reviews.author: Amanda the Jedi

reviews.text: Östlund sets sail into new waters, delivering a thought-provoking, grotesque and biting satire about the eternal class struggle. [Full Review in Spanish]
reviews.author: Rene Sanchez

reviews.text: There are subtle little gags scattered between the more obvious ones... but overall the satire is scattershot.
reviews.author: Raphael Abraham

reviews.text: Utterly unhinged in the best way possible, guaranteed to elicit enough laughter to make your stomach ache, while also leaving you with plenty to think about afterwards.
reviews.author: Alysha Prasad

reviews.text: What first appears to be a look at the rich and luxurious lifestyle of being a model and an influencer, "Triangle Of Sadness" takes Östlund's satirical formula to another level in a film that lacks subtlety but in the best way possible.
reviews.author: Amy Smith

reviews.text: Triangle Of Sadness takes it to the next level, and bids fair to win big too.
reviews.author: Shubhra Gupta

reviews.text: Triangle of Sadness exhibits an updated vocabulary that speaks to the relationship between an evolving social hierarchy and the firm persistence of this hierarchy itself.
reviews.author: Morris Yang

reviews.text: A very black satire on the stupidity of the superficiality of our times... A portrait of the human decay of a rotten soul when it loses its own perspective. [Full review in Spanish]
reviews.author: Sara Martínez Ruiz

reviews.text: When it works, this thing is a beast. This applies especially to the mid-section of the film, which is rich, observant, biting, outrageous -- satirical comedy at its finest.
reviews.author: Zhuo-Ning Su

reviews.text: The script could’ve been tighter, but Triangle of Sadness keeps the laughs coming thick and fast, even well into the home stretch. Who knew class politics could be this much fun?
reviews.author: Ryan Leston

reviews.text: The narrative is wrecked when the yacht sinks and the survivors must make do on a seemingly uninhabited island. At that moment, Östlund's class observations become more superficial and the story drags on to an open end. [Full review in Spanish]
reviews.author: Leonardo Garcia Tsao

reviews.text: Ruben Östlund’s takedown of the super-rich that plays like Buñuel by way of the Farrelly brothers.
reviews.author: Philip De Semlyen

reviews.text: so simplistic... the alleged political speculation ends up in the greatest of all obviousness.
reviews.author: Carlos F. Heredero

reviews.text: Ruben Östlund is clearly having the time of his life with this cinematic chorus of Eat the Rich! The fun is infectious, and despite an indulgence with regards to the runtime this is a beautiful, and very funny film.
reviews.author: Jo-Ann Titmarsh

reviews.text: Östlund has created a full-throated, roaring comedy of hate against the upper-classes. It is cynical, nihilistic and has no issue about punching down, though it spends most of its time punching up, aiming squarely.
reviews.author: John Bleasdale

reviews.text: Subtlety is not the primary aim in this film’s portrayal of class — and it’s a nasty hoot because of it.
reviews.author: Iana Murray

reviews.text: A scatological rinsing of wealth and hubris from a filmmaker who, with each passing effort, only further cements himself as contemporary cinema’s auteur of such things.
reviews.author: Rory O'Connor

reviews.text: The formula works, the dialogues are drilled at impossible speeds and the black humor expands like gas. [Full Review in Spanish]
reviews.author: Mariona Borrull

reviews.text: In the past, Östlund has shown a deft facility in sending up meaty topics... Here, however, he stoops to the broadness ascribed to his work by its harshest critics, now more parody of himself than parodist.
reviews.author: Charles Bramesco

reviews.text: It’s very much on brand for Östlund to explore surface level aesthetics through a moral lens; but it’s the moral of the perceiver that often falls prey to his meta-satirical treatment.
reviews.author: Savina Petkova

reviews.text: It's certainly an enjoyable watch, but not quite as well-executed as Force Majeure or The Square.
reviews.author: Hannah Strong

reviews.text: The director of The Square gives a new shape a whirl with hilarious, scathing and sometimes jaw-dropping results.
reviews.author: Neil Smith

reviews.text: “Triangle of Sadness” feels both bloated and slight, stretching out a shrewd but limited thesis that all the world’s a market about as far it will go, and then running back the tape and doing it again.
reviews.author: Ben Croll

reviews.text: Triangle of Sadness is a two-and-a-half-hour joke-a-minute biting satire of the rich and class that keeps you guessing in every scene. An incredible cast of characters that I’m gonna miss hanging out with. I could have watched it for hours.
reviews.author: Karl Delossantos

reviews.text: It’s Parasite meets Ghost Ship (and that’s a good thing). Triangle of Sadness is a total delight.
reviews.author: Catherine Bray

reviews.text: Ruben Östlund once again crafts a jet black comedy, this one an excoriation of class, privilege and lack of competence or bodily control, a LORD OF THE FOOLS seasick parable about the fragility the social contract. What bleak, blissful, fun
reviews.author: Jason Gorber

reviews.text: Begins as a fairly lightweight critique of the modelling industry but slowly builds into a panoramic takedown of capitalism, patriarchy, tax evasion, structural racism, the class system, white privilege, Instagram influencers and pretentious fine dining.
reviews.author: Stephen Dalton

reviews.text: Triangle of Sadness needn’t be a fair film... A more carefully shaped argument would have been appreciated, though. And one that didn’t dissolve so quickly into a juvenile snicker.
reviews.author: Richard Lawson

reviews.text: Even by Östlund’s own output, his latest tends to feel a bit self-indulgent, but it’s more often than not a lot of subversive fun.
reviews.author: Nicholas Bell

reviews.text: If not for de Leon’s bold and heartsick performance, Triangle of Sadness would fail to achieve any real measure of the physical discomfort that has animated so much of Östlund’s previous work.
reviews.author: David Ehrlich

reviews.text: A biting satire that explodes into absolute chaos.
reviews.author: Rafael Motamayor

reviews.text: [A] rather laborious take on the excesses of capitalism...
reviews.author: Jonathan Romney

reviews.text: Strident, derivative and dismayingly deficient in genuine laughs...
reviews.author: Peter Bradshaw

reviews.text: Who could resist a film in which a sweet old lady watches a live grenade roll down the deck and come to a rest against her foot, then turns to her husband and says: “Look, dear, it’s one of ours”?
reviews.author: Robbie Collin

reviews.text: [A] disappointingly blunt satire of class and status...
reviews.author: David Rooney

reviews.text: The thing about Östlund is that he makes you laugh, but he also makes you think.
reviews.author: Peter Debruge

synopsis: In Ruben Östlund's wickedly funny Palme d'Or winner, social hierarchy is turned upside down, revealing the tawdry relationship between power and beauty. Celebrity model couple, Carl (Harris Dickinson) and Yaya (Charlbi Dean), are invited on a luxury cruise for the uber-rich, helmed by an unhinged boat captain (Woody Harrelson). What first appeared instagrammable ends catastrophically, leaving the survivors stranded on a desert island and fighting for survival.
